items.title: Louie Bellson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Bud Hobgood. He was the one that arranged the recording session.

ctx.x: . . . how did it work? You just played the music down for him? How did the session go?

Yeah. We played it down once for him. He had it. He was so wrapped up with the band. The sound of the band knocked him out completely, because that band was hot. That band was – they were ready. They ate up those things. We had one short rehearsal with just Oliver, to check it, to see if there were any bad notes. He cleared that off. It was amazing to me that James Brown was able to get into the swing things and also into his own bag, his bag of singing. The same thing with the band. Everything just jelled. No…
What did Maceo do? What was his role in that? Because he usually served as musical director for the James Brown band. So what was his role in this project?
